sanskrit: taṃ sātyakir bhīmaseno dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ abhyadravanta bhīṣmasya rathaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam
english: At him rushed Sātyaki, Bhīmasena, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata, charging upon Bhīṣma's chariot adorned with gold.

sanskrit: parivārya ca te sarve gāṅgeyaṃ rabhasaṃ raṇe tribhis tribhiḥ śarair ghorair bhīṣmam ānarchur añjasā
english: Surrounding on every side the impetuous son of Gaṅgā in the fray, they all swiftly struck Bhīṣma, each with three terrible arrows.

sanskrit: pratyavidhyata tān sarvān pitā devavratas tava yatamānān maheṣvāsāṃs tribhis tribhir ajihmagaiḥ
english: Your father Devavrata pierced them all in return—those great bowmen straining at their utmost—with three straight-flying shafts apiece.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasreṇa saṃnivārya mahārathān hayān kāñcanasaṃnāhān bhīmasya nyahanac charaiḥ
english: Then, holding off those mighty car-warriors with a thousand arrows, he slew with his shafts Bhīma's steeds caparisoned in golden trappings.

sanskrit: hatāśve tu rathe tiṣṭhan bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān śaktiṃ cikṣepa tarasā gāṅgeyasya rathaṃ prati
english: Standing in his chariot whose horses were slain, the valorous Bhīmasena hurled a lance with force against the chariot of the son of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: aprāptām eva tāṃ śaktiṃ pitā devavratas tava tridhā ciccheda samare sā pṛthivyām aśīryata
english: That lance, before ever it reached him, your father Devavrata cut into three in the battle, and it fell shattered to the earth.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaikyāyasīṃ gurvīṃ pragṛhya balavad gadām bhīmaseno rathāt tūrṇaṃ pupluve manujarṣabha
english: Then, seizing a heavy mace of tempered iron, the mighty Bhīmasena leaped swiftly down from his chariot, O bull among men.

sanskrit: sātyako 'pi tatas tūrṇaṃ bhīmasya priyakāmyayā sārathiṃ kuruvṛddhasya pātayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: And Sātyaki too, at once, wishing to please Bhīma, brought down with his shafts the charioteer of the aged Kuru.

sanskrit: bhīṣmas tu nihate tasmin sārathau rathināṃ varaḥ vātāyamānais tair aśvair apanīto raṇājirāt
english: But Bhīṣma, foremost of car-warriors, when his charioteer was slain, was carried off from the field of battle by those horses that ran like the wind.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tato rājann apanīte mahāvrate prajajvāla yathā vahnir dahan kakṣam ivaidhitaḥ
english: Then, O king, when he of the great vows had been borne away, Bhīmasena blazed up like a fire grown high as it consumes dry brushwood.

sanskrit: sa hatvā sarvakāliṅgān senāmadhye vyatiṣṭhata nainam abhyutsahan ke cit tāvakā bharatarṣabha
english: Having slain all the Kaliṅgas, he stood in the midst of the host, and none of your warriors dared confront him, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tam āropya svarathe rathināṃ varaḥ paśyatāṃ sarvasainyānām apovāha yaśasvinam
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna, foremost of car-warriors, taking the illustrious one up into his own chariot, bore him away in the sight of all the armies.

sanskrit: saṃpūjyamānaḥ pāñcālyair matsyaiś ca bharatarṣabha dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ pariṣvajya sameyād atha sātyakim
english: Honored by the Pāñcālas and the Matsyas, O bull of the Bhāratas, having embraced Dhṛṣṭadyumna, he then came to Sātyaki.

sanskrit: athābravīd bhīmasenaṃ sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ praharṣayan yaduvyāghro dhṛṣṭadyumnasya paśyataḥ
english: Then Sātyaki of true valor, the tiger of the Yadus, gladdening him, spoke to Bhīmasena while Dhṛṣṭadyumna looked on:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā kaliṅgarājaś ca rājaputraś ca ketumān śakradevaś ca kāliṅgaḥ kaliṅgāś ca mṛdhe hatāḥ
english: By good fortune the king of the Kaliṅgas, and the prince Ketumān, and Śakradeva the Kaliṅga, and the Kaliṅgas themselves are slain in the fight.

sanskrit: svabāhubalavīryeṇa nāgāśvarathasaṃkulaḥ mahāvyūhaḥ kaliṅgānām ekena mṛditas tvayā
english: By the strength and valor of your own arm, the great battle-array of the Kaliṅgas, thronged with elephants, horses, and chariots, has been crushed by you alone.

sanskrit: evam uktvā śiner naptā dīrghabāhur ariṃdamaḥ rathād ratham abhidrutya paryaṣvajata pāṇḍavam
english: Having spoken thus, the long-armed grandson of Śini, the tamer of foes, springing from chariot to chariot, embraced the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tataḥ svaratham āruhya punar eva mahārathaḥ tāvakān avadhīt kruddho bhīmasya balam ādadhat
english: Then, mounting his own chariot once more, that great car-warrior, enraged, slew your men, lending strength to Bhīma's force.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca gatāparāhṇabhūyiṣṭhe tasminn ahani bhārata rathanāgāśvapattīnāṃ sādināṃ ca mahākṣaye
english: Saṃjaya said: When the greater part of the afternoon of that day had passed, O Bhārata, amid the great destruction of chariots, elephants, horses, foot-soldiers, and cavalry,

sanskrit: droṇaputreṇa śalyena kṛpeṇa ca mahātmanā samasajjata pāñcālyas tribhir etair mahārathaiḥ
english: the prince of Pāñcāla engaged with these three great car-warriors—the son of Droṇa, Śalya, and the high-souled Kṛpa.

sanskrit: sa lokaviditān aśvān nijaghāna mahābalaḥ drauṇeḥ pāñcāladāyādaḥ śitair daśabhir āśugaiḥ
english: That mighty heir of the Pāñcālas struck down the world-famed steeds of the son of Droṇa with ten sharp, swift-flying arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ śalyarathaṃ tūrṇam āsthāya hatavāhanaḥ drauṇiḥ pāñcāladāyādam abhyavarṣad atheṣubhiḥ
english: Then the son of Droṇa, his horses slain, quickly mounted Śalya's chariot and rained arrows upon the heir of the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tu saṃsaktaṃ drauṇinā dṛśya bhārata saubhadro 'bhyapatat tūrṇaṃ vikiran niśitāñ śarān
english: Seeing Dhṛṣṭadyumna locked in combat with the son of Droṇa, O Bhārata, the son of Subhadrā rushed up at once, scattering whetted shafts.

sanskrit: sa śalyaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā kṛpaṃ ca navabhiḥ śaraiḥ aśvatthāmānam aṣṭābhir vivyādha puruṣarṣabha
english: He pierced Śalya with twenty-five arrows, Kṛpa with nine, and Aśvatthāman with eight, O bull among men.

sanskrit: ārjuniṃ tu tatas tūrṇaṃ drauṇir vivyādha patriṇā śalyo dvādaśabhiś caiva kṛpaś ca niśitais tribhiḥ
english: Then the son of Droṇa swiftly pierced the son of Arjuna with a feathered shaft, Śalya with twelve, and Kṛpa with three whetted arrows.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇas tava pautras tu tava pautram avasthitam abhyavartata saṃhṛṣṭas tato yuddham avartata
english: And Lakṣmaṇa, your grandson, advanced exultantly against your grandson who stood there, and thereupon a battle ensued.

sanskrit: dauryodhanis tu saṃkruddhaḥ saubhadraṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha samare rājaṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Then Duryodhana's son, full of wrath, pierced the son of Subhadrā with nine arrows in the fight, O king, and it seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: abhimanyus tu saṃkruddho bhrātaraṃ bharatarṣabha śaraiḥ pañcāśatā rājan kṣiprahasto 'bhyavidhyata
english: But Abhimanyu, enraged, O bull of the Bhāratas, quick of hand, pierced his cousin with fifty arrows, O king.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇo 'pi tatas tasya dhanuś ciccheda patriṇā muṣṭideśe mahārāja tata uccukruśur janāḥ
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa with a feathered shaft cut his bow at the grip, O great king, and at that the people raised a great shout.

sanskrit: tad vihāya dhanuś chinnaṃ saubhadraḥ paravīrahā anyad ādattavāṃś citraṃ kārmukaṃ vegavattaram
english: Casting aside that severed bow, the son of Subhadrā, slayer of hostile heroes, took up another splendid bow of swifter force.

sanskrit: tau tatra samare hṛṣṭau kṛtapratikṛtaiṣiṇau anyonyaṃ viśikhais tīkṣṇair jaghnatuḥ puruṣarṣabhau
english: Those two bulls among men, eager in that battle, each seeking to repay the other blow for blow, struck one another with sharp, keen arrows.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā dṛṣṭvā putraṃ mahāratham pīḍitaṃ tava pautreṇa prāyāt tatra janeśvaraḥ
english: Then King Duryodhana, lord of men, seeing his son, that great car-warrior, hard pressed by your grandson, went thither.

sanskrit: saṃnivṛtte tava sute sarva eva janādhipāḥ ārjuniṃ rathavaṃśena samantāt paryavārayan
english: When your son had turned to the fight, all the lords of men hemmed in the son of Arjuna on every side with their array of chariots.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛtaḥ śūraiḥ śūro yudhi sudurjayaiḥ na sma vivyathate rājan kṛṣṇatulyaparākramaḥ
english: Surrounded by those heroes, hard to conquer in battle, that hero, whose prowess equaled Kṛṣṇa's, was not shaken at all, O king.

sanskrit: saubhadram atha saṃsaktaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā dhanaṃjayaḥ abhidudrāva saṃkruddhas trātukāmaḥ svam ātmajam
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya, seeing the son of Subhadrā locked in combat there, rushed forward in fury, longing to rescue his own son.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarathanāgāśvā bhīṣmadroṇapurogamāḥ abhyavartanta rājānaḥ sahitāḥ savyasācinam
english: Then the kings, with their chariots, elephants, and horses, led by Bhīṣma and Droṇa, advanced together against Savyasācin.

sanskrit: uddhūtaṃ sahasā bhaumaṃ nāgāśvarathasādibhiḥ divākarapathaṃ prāpya rajas tīvram adṛśyata
english: The dust of the earth, suddenly thrown up by elephants, horses, chariots, and cavalry, rose dense to the path of the sun and was seen on high.

sanskrit: tāni nāgasahasrāṇi bhūmipālaśatāni ca tasya bāṇapathaṃ prāpya nābhyavartanta sarvaśaḥ
english: Those thousands of elephants and hundreds of kings, coming within the range of his arrows, could in no way press forward.

sanskrit: praṇeduḥ sarvabhūtāni babhūvus timirā diśaḥ kurūṇām anayas tīvraḥ samadṛśyata dāruṇaḥ
english: All creatures wailed, the quarters grew dark, and a fierce, dreadful calamity of the Kurus was plainly seen.

sanskrit: nāpy antarikṣaṃ na diśo na bhūmir na ca bhāskaraḥ prajajñe bharataśreṣṭha śarasaṃghaiḥ kirīṭinaḥ
english: Neither the sky, nor the quarters, nor the earth, nor the sun could be made out, O best of the Bhāratas, for the masses of arrows loosed by the diademed one.

sanskrit: sāditadhvajanāgās tu hatāśvā rathino bhṛśam vipradrutarathāḥ ke cid dṛśyante rathayūthapāḥ
english: Some leaders of chariot-bands were seen with their banners and elephants brought low, their steeds slain, the warriors sorely stricken, their chariots scattered in flight.

sanskrit: virathā rathinaś cānye dhāvamānāḥ samantataḥ tatra tatraiva dṛśyante sāyudhāḥ sāṅgadair bhujaiḥ
english: Other car-warriors, deprived of their chariots, were seen here and there running on every side, still bearing their weapons, with armlets upon their arms.

sanskrit: hayārohā hayāṃs tyaktvā gajārohāś ca dantinaḥ arjunasya bhayād rājan samantād vipradudruvuḥ
english: Riders abandoning their horses, and mahouts their tusked beasts, fled in every direction out of fear of Arjuna, O king.

sanskrit: rathebhyaś ca gajebhyaś ca hayebhyaś ca narādhipāḥ patitāḥ pātyamānāś ca dṛśyante 'rjunatāḍitāḥ
english: Lords of men, struck by Arjuna, were seen fallen and falling from their chariots, their elephants, and their horses.

sanskrit: sagadān udyatān bāhūn sakhaḍgāṃś ca viśāṃ pate saprāsāṃś ca satūṇīrān saśarān saśarāsanān
english: Arms raised on high, grasping maces and swords, O lord of the people, holding lances and quivers, arrows and bows,

sanskrit: sāṅkuśān sapatākāṃś ca tatra tatrārjuno nṛṇām nicakarta śarair ugrai raudraṃ bibhrad vapus tadā
english: and goads and standards—these of the warriors Arjuna hewed off here and there with his fierce arrows, wearing then a dreadful form.

sanskrit: parighāṇāṃ pravṛddhānāṃ mudgarāṇāṃ ca māriṣa prāsānāṃ bhiṇḍipālānāṃ nistriṃśānāṃ ca saṃyuge
english: Of massive iron clubs and of war-hammers, my lord, of lances and slings and swords in the battle,

sanskrit: paraśvadhānāṃ tīkṣṇānāṃ tomarāṇāṃ ca bhārata varmaṇāṃ cāpaviddhānāṃ kavacānāṃ ca bhūtale
english: of sharp battle-axes and javelins, O Bhārata, and of shattered mail-coats and cuirasses upon the ground,

sanskrit: dhvajānāṃ carmaṇāṃ caiva vyajanānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ chatrāṇāṃ hemadaṇḍānāṃ cāmarāṇāṃ ca bhārata
english: of banners and shields and fans on every side, of parasols with golden staves and yak-tail whisks, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: pratodānāṃ kaśānāṃ ca yoktrāṇāṃ caiva māriṣa rāśayaś cātra dṛśyante vinikīrṇā raṇakṣitau
english: and of goads and whips and harness-straps, my lord—heaps of these were seen strewn there upon the field of battle.

sanskrit: nāsīt tatra pumān kaś cit tava sainyasya bhārata yo 'rjunaṃ samare śūraṃ pratyudyāyāt kathaṃ cana
english: There was not a single man of your army, O Bhārata, who could in any wise advance against the heroic Arjuna in battle.

sanskrit: yo yo hi samare pārthaṃ patyudyāti viśāṃ pate sa sa vai viśikhais tīkṣṇaiḥ paralokāya nīyate
english: For whoever advanced against Pārtha in the fight, O lord of the people, he was sent to the other world by his sharp shafts.

sanskrit: teṣu vidravamāṇeṣu tava yodheṣu sarvaśaḥ arjuno vāsudevaś ca dadhmatur vārijottamau
english: As your warriors fled in every direction, Arjuna and Vāsudeva blew their excellent conches.

sanskrit: tat prabhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitā devavratas tava abravīt samare śūraṃ bhāradvājaṃ smayann iva
english: Seeing that host broken, your father Devavrata spoke in the battle to the hero, the son of Bhāradvāja, as if with a smile:

sanskrit: eṣa pāṇḍusuto vīraḥ kṛṣṇena sahito balī tathā karoti sainyāni yathā kuryād dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: This heroic son of Pāṇḍu, joined with Kṛṣṇa, the mighty one, deals with the armies just as Dhanaṃjaya would.

sanskrit: na hy eṣa samare śakyo jetum adya kathaṃ cana yathāsya dṛśyate rūpaṃ kālāntakayamopamam
english: For he can in no way be conquered today in battle, since the form he wears appears like Yama the all-ending Death.

sanskrit: na nivartayituṃ cāpi śakyeyaṃ mahatī camūḥ anyonyaprekṣayā paśya dravatīyaṃ varūthinī
english: Nor can this great host be turned back: behold, this army flees, each man only watching the other run.

sanskrit: eṣa cāstaṃ giriśreṣṭhaṃ bhānumān pratipadyate vapūṃṣi sarvalokasya saṃharann iva sarvathā
english: And the sun is now reaching the best of mountains, where it sets, as if withdrawing utterly the forms of all the world.

sanskrit: tatrāvahāraṃ saṃprāptaṃ manye 'haṃ puruṣarṣabha śrāntā bhītāś ca no yodhā na yotsyanti kathaṃ cana
english: I think the hour for withdrawal has come, O bull among men; our warriors, weary and afraid, will not fight at all.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato bhīṣmo droṇam ācāryasattamam avahāram atho cakre tāvakānāṃ mahārathaḥ
english: Having spoken thus to Droṇa, the best of teachers, Bhīṣma, that great car-warrior, then ordered the withdrawal of your forces.

sanskrit: tato 'vahāraḥ sainyānāṃ tava teṣāṃ ca bhārata astaṃ gacchati sūrye 'bhūt saṃdhyākāle ca vartati
english: Then came the withdrawal of the armies, both yours and theirs, O Bhārata, as the sun went down and the hour of twilight set in.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavas tataḥ anīkāny anusaṃyāne vyādideśātha bhārata
english: Saṃjaya said: When the night had brightened into dawn, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu then gave orders for the marshalling of the troops, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: gāruḍaṃ ca mahāvyūhaṃ cakre śāṃtanavas tadā putrāṇāṃ te jayākāṅkṣī bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ
english: And the son of Śaṃtanu then formed the great battle-array of the Garuḍa, Bhīṣma, the grandsire of the Kurus, longing for the victory of your sons.

sanskrit: garuḍasya svayaṃ tuṇḍe pitā devavratas tava cakṣuṣī ca bharadvājaḥ kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ
english: At Garuḍa's beak was your father Devavrata himself; as its two eyes were the son of Bhāradvāja and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvatas.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva śīrṣam āstāṃ yaśasvinau trigartair matsyakaikeyair vāṭadhānaiś ca saṃyutau
english: Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa, the two illustrious ones, stood at the head, joined by the Trigartas, the Matsyas, the Kekayas, and the Vāṭadhānas.

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ śalaḥ śalyo bhagadattaś ca māriṣa madrakāḥ sindhusauvīrās tathā pañcanadāś ca ye
english: Bhūriśravas, Śala, Śalya, and Bhagadatta, my lord, the Madrakas, the Sindhu-Sauvīras, and the men of the Five Rivers,

sanskrit: jayadrathena sahitā grīvāyāṃ saṃniveśitāḥ pṛṣṭhe duryodhano rājā sodaraiḥ sānugair vṛtaḥ
english: together with Jayadratha, were stationed at the neck; at the back was King Duryodhana, surrounded by his brothers and his followers.

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau kāmbojaś ca śakaiḥ saha puccham āsan mahārāja śūrasenāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, and the Kāmboja chief with the Śakas, formed the tail, O great king, and the Śūrasenas as well in their entirety.

sanskrit: māgadhāś ca kaliṅgāś ca dāśerakagaṇaiḥ saha dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣam āsādya sthitā vyūhasya daṃśitāḥ
english: The Māgadhas and the Kaliṅgas, with the hosts of the Dāśerakas, taking up the right wing of the array, stood there clad in armor.

sanskrit: kānanāś ca vikuñjāś ca muktāḥ puṇḍrāviṣas tathā bṛhadbalena sahitā vāmaṃ pakṣam upāśritāḥ
english: The Kānanas and the Vikuñjas, the Muktas, and the Puṇḍrāviṣas, together with Bṛhadbala, took up the left wing.

sanskrit: vyūḍhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu tat sainyaṃ savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnena sahitaḥ pratyavyūhata saṃyuge ardhacandreṇa vyūhena vyūhaṃ tam atidāruṇam
english: Seeing that host marshalled, Savyasācin, the scorcher of foes, together with Dhṛṣṭadyumna, drew up his counter-array in the battle, opposing that most terrible formation with an array in the shape of a crescent moon.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇaṃ śṛṅgam āsthāya bhīmaseno vyarocata nānāśastraughasaṃpannair nānādeśyair nṛpair vṛtaḥ
english: Holding the right horn, Bhīmasena shone resplendent, surrounded by kings of many lands furnished with floods of diverse weapons.

sanskrit: tad anv eva virāṭaś ca drupadaś ca mahārathaḥ tadanantaram evāsīn nīlo nīlāyudhaiḥ saha
english: Next to him came Virāṭa and Drupada, the great car-warrior; and immediately after them stood Nīla with his blue-armored troops.

sanskrit: nīlād anantaraṃ caiva dhṛṣṭaketur mahārathaḥ cedikāśikarūṣaiś ca pauravaiś cābhisaṃvṛtaḥ
english: Next after Nīla stood Dhṛṣṭaketu, the great car-warrior, encompassed by the Cedis, the Kāśis, the Karūṣas, and the Pauravas.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca pāñcālāś ca prabhadrakāḥ madhye sainyasya mahataḥ sthitā yuddhāya bhārata
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, with the Pāñcālas and the Prabhadrakas, stood in the center of the great host, ready for battle, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tathaiva dharmarājo 'pi gajānīkena saṃvṛtaḥ tatas tu sātyakī rājan draupadyāḥ pañca cātmajāḥ
english: Likewise the King of Righteousness, encompassed by his division of elephants; and then, O king, Sātyaki and the five sons of Draupadī.

sanskrit: abhimanyus tatas tūrṇam irāvāṃś ca tataḥ param bhaimasenis tato rājan kekayāś ca mahārathāḥ
english: Then Abhimanyu close at hand, and Irāvat beyond him, and then the son of Bhīmasena, O king, and the Kekaya princes, those great car-warriors.

sanskrit: tato 'bhūd dvipadāṃ śreṣṭho vāmaṃ pārśvam upāśritaḥ sarvasya jagato goptā goptā yasya janārdanaḥ
english: Then the best of two-footed beings took the left flank, the guardian of all the world, whose own guardian was Janārdana.

sanskrit: evam etan mahāvyūhaṃ pratyavyūhanta pāṇḍavāḥ vadhārthaṃ tava putrāṇāṃ tatpakṣaṃ ye ca saṃgatāḥ
english: Thus did the Pāṇḍavas draw up this great counter-array, for the destruction of your sons and of those who had joined their side.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ vyatiṣaktarathadvipam tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca nighnatām itaretaram
english: Then the battle began, with chariots and elephants entangled together, as your men and the foe struck down one another.
